provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Jesus loves children
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state that Jesus loves children.
The pupils should be able to explain why children are important to Jesus.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about Jesus' birth. Today we learn how Jesus shows special love to children.

Content:
Jesus said 'Let the children come to me' in Mark 10:14. This shows children matter to Jesus. Jesus used children as an example of how to enter heaven. Like when a mother brought her child to Jesus, he welcomed the child. Jesus loves all children in Nigeria, whether in Lagos or in a small village.

Class activity:
Each pupil will draw a picture of themselves with Jesus and write one way Jesus loves them.

Evaluation questions:
1. What did Jesus say about children?
2. How did Jesus show love to children?
3. Why do you think Jesus loves children?

Summary:
Jesus loves every child and wants us to come to him just as we are.

topics.title: Jesus heals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify stories where Jesus healed people.
The pupils should be able to explain how caring for the sick pleases Jesus.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Jesus' love for children. Today we learn how Jesus made sick people well.

Content:
Jesus healed many people in the Bible. He healed a man who could not walk, a woman with blood issue, and a blind man. Jesus showed compassion when healing. He touched people and spoke kindly to them. In Nigeria, when someone is sick like with malaria or typhoid, we care for them like Jesus cares for us.

Class activity:
Pupils will role-play visiting a sick friend and bringing them fruit or water.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one person Jesus healed.
2. How did Jesus show love when healing?
3. What can we do when someone is sick?

Summary:
Jesus has power to heal and wants us to care for those who are sick.

topics.title: Jesus teaches kindness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of the good Samaritan.
The pupils should be able to list ways to be a good neighbour.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Jesus healing the sick. Today we learn about Jesus teaching us to be kind to others.

Content:
Jesus told the story of the good Samaritan. A man was robbed and hurt. A priest and Levite passed by but did not help. A Samaritan stopped, helped him, and paid for his care. Jesus said we should be like the good Samaritan. In our market or compound, we can help people who need help, just like the good Samaritan helped the hurt man.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs to list three ways they can help someone in need this week.

Evaluation questions:
1. Who stopped to help the hurt man in the story?
2. What did the good Samaritan do for the hurt man?
3. How can you be a good neighbour to your friend?

Summary:
Jesus teaches us to show kindness to everyone, even people who are different from us.

topics.title: The lost sheep
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recount the story of the lost sheep.
The pupils should be able to explain that God never gives up on anyone.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about being kind neighbours. Today we learn about how much God cares for every one of us.

Content:
Jesus told a story about a shepherd with 100 sheep. One sheep wandered away and got lost. The shepherd left the 99 sheep to search for the lost one. When he found it, he was happy and carried it home. This story shows that God loves each person like the shepherd loved his sheep. Even if you feel lost like a sheep in the harmattan fog, God will find you.

Class activity:
Pupils will play a game where one pupil is the lost sheep and others help find them.

Evaluation questions:
1. How many sheep were with the shepherd?
2. What did the shepherd do when one sheep was lost?
3. Why do you think God compares us to sheep?

Summary:
God loves every person and will never give up on finding us when we are lost.

topics.title: The generous boy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of Jesus feeding 5000.
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of sharing with others.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about the lost sheep. Today we learn about how Jesus used a small boy's gift to feed many people.

Content:
Jesus was teaching a large crowd of 5000 men plus women and children. They were hungry. A boy had five small loaves and two small fish. Jesus took the food, gave thanks, and divided it. Everyone ate until they were full with 12 baskets of leftovers left. This shows how Jesus can use small things when we share them. Like sharing your naira to buy snacks for friends, Jesus can multiply our giving.

Class activity:
Pupils will bring a small snack to share with three other classmates.

Evaluation questions:
1. What food did the boy have to share?
2. How many people ate from the boy's small gift?
3. What happens when we share what we have with others?

Summary:
When we share what little we have, Jesus can do great things with it.

topics.title: Jesus and prayer
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the Lord's prayer.
The pupils should be able to list different times to pray each day.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about sharing with others. Today we learn about talking to God through prayer.

Content:
Jesus taught his disciples how to pray. The Lord's prayer begins with 'Our Father who art in heaven'. We should pray every morning when we wake up, before meals, and before sleeping. Jesus often went to quiet places to pray. In Nigeria, we can pray before eating our rice, before going to school, and before sleeping in our room. Prayer is talking to God like talking to your father.

Class activity:
Pupils will write a simple prayer to pray before their next meal.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the first line of the Lord's prayer?
2. When should we pray each day?
3. Why is prayer important for Christians?

Summary:
Jesus teaches us to pray regularly and trust God with our needs.

topics.title: Giving thanks
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of the ten lepers.
The pupils should be able to identify things to thank God for.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about prayer. Today we learn about the importance of saying thank you to God.

Content:
Jesus healed ten men with leprosy. Only one came back to thank him. Jesus asked where the other nine were. We should always thank God for what he does for us. In Nigeria, we can thank God for our food, our family, and good health like when we recover from sickness. Saying thank you shows we remember God's goodness.

Class activity:
Pupils will make a list of five things they are thankful for this week.

Evaluation questions:
1. How many men did Jesus heal?
2. How many men came back to thank Jesus?
3. What are three things you can thank God for today?

Summary:
We should always remember to thank God for his blessings in our lives.

topics.title: Honesty pleases God
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify what the Bible says about stealing and lying.
The pupils should be able to explain why honesty is important.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about giving thanks. Today we learn about being honest in what we say and do.

Content:
The Bible tells us not to steal or lie. These are sins that make God sad. When we are honest, people trust us like they trust a good market seller who gives correct change. Being honest means telling the truth even when it is hard. Like returning extra naira if a shopkeeper gives you too much change. God is pleased when we are truthful in all we do.

Class activity:
Pupils will write one honest promise they will keep this week.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does the Bible say about stealing?
2. Why is it important to tell the truth?
3. Give an example of being honest in school.

Summary:
God is pleased when we choose to be honest in our words and actions.

topics.title: The prodigal son
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of the prodigal son.
The pupils should be able to explain that God welcomes us back when we say sorry.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about honesty. Today we learn about saying sorry and receiving forgiveness.

Content:
Jesus told a story of a son who asked his father for his share of wealth. He wasted it all on bad living. When he had nothing, he decided to return home. His father saw him coming and ran to welcome him back. The father forgave him and threw a party. This shows God welcomes us back when we are truly sorry. Like when a child comes back to their compound after making mistakes, God welcomes us with love.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture of the father welcoming the son home.

Evaluation questions:
1. What did the son do with his money?
2. How did the father react when his son returned?
3. What does this story teach us about God?

Summary:
God is always ready to forgive us and welcome us back when we are truly sorry.

topics.title: Revision and memory verses
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite memory verses from this term.
The pupils should be able to sing praise songs about God's love.

Introduction:
This week we will review all we have learned this term and celebrate with songs.

Content:
We have learned many Bible stories this term about Jesus' love, healing, kindness, and forgiveness. Let us remember our memory verses like 'Let the children come to me' and 'Love your neighbour as yourself'. We can sing songs like 'Jesus loves me' and 'This little light of mine'. We should remember these lessons all year.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to create a short drama about one story they learned this term.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one memory verse from this term.
2. What story about Jesus did you like most this term?
3. How will you show God's love to others next week?

Summary:
Let us keep God's word in our hearts and share his love with everyone.
